svg.title: sidecar services
svg.desc: Encrypted storage: Git repos and file trees, encrypted on your device: paths, names, messages and contents. Stock git still works, and subscribers hear of changes in real time.; Group keys: Each repo is an MLS group with post-quantum hybrid keys. Members' devices hold the keys, agents get wrapped copies, and removing anyone rotates them.; Agent record: One MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and any harness. Every session and changed file lands in your encrypted vault, every approval as a signed receipt.; Email and burners: Your own mail server, with unlimited aliases and burner addresses. Inbound TLS ends on your indexer, outbound TLS runs to the recipient, and the edges keep nothing.; Public HTTPS: Publish a local app at app.<net>.ur.network with an automatic certificate. The edge routes by SNI and never decrypts, and the key stays on your machine.; Private network: A stable private address and name for every device and agent. Subnet routes and port forwards are granted by your access policy and carried end to end.; Sockets and sharing: Listen on a name instead of a port, and each dial reaches one listener, chosen by load. File-share links work a set number of times.; Teams and access: Members, roles, SSO, and enrollment by QR code or MDM. A deny-by-default policy is signed into your encrypted config and evaluated on every device.; Encrypted search: Each repo keeps an encrypted index its committers update. Search mail, notes and code, or find agents working on a task, and the server never sees your queries.
